concepts.text: Tuned mass absorber tuned to 1.9 Hz — sprung steel mass under deck supplying inertial counteracting force (Millennium Bridge 26 pairs vertical absorbers 1-3 t, mass ratio 3-5% per Cambridge ICSV review)
concepts.author: Structural Dynamicist

concepts.text: Under-deck vertical coil-spring plus linear guide suspension that converts bridge vertical motion into large relative mass travel (Millennium vertical tuned absorbers on transoms per Cambridge ICSV review)
concepts.author: Structural Dynamicist

concepts.text: Viscous dashpot in TMD tuned to Den Hartog optimum damping ratio sqrt(3 mu/8(1+mu)) — converts relative motion to heat at small amplitudes
concepts.author: Structural Dynamicist

concepts.text: Steel bracket frame bolting TMD units to main girders at midspan antinode, carrying inertia plus static weight into primary structure

concepts.text: Elastomeric end stops plus caged travel gap sized beyond design TMD stroke to catch over-travel during crowd surge or detuning
concepts.author: Structural Dynamicist

concepts.text: Conceal all TMD hardware below deck soffit attached to girders leaving deck sightline and walkway untouched (Millennium constraint: appearance unchanged per Cambridge review, mods out of sight under deck)
concepts.author: Structural Dynamicist

concepts.text: Added under-deck stiffness alternative — paired longitudinal stiffener ribs plus transverse diaphragms under soffit raising bending frequency out of walking band, versus pure added damping (stiffening-vs-damping tradeoff for 40 m span)
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

concepts.text: HSFG-clamped under-deck bracket frame — preloaded High-Strength Friction-Grip bolts clamping TMD and damper reactions into main girders at midspan antinode without welding, sized for inertia plus static weight; assumed_constraint: total added dead load under 2% of pedestrian live load
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

concepts.text: Midspan under-deck mounting at first-mode antinode — all absorber and damper units grouped within middle third of 40 m span where vertical bending motion is largest
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

concepts.text: Supplemental viscous damper working in parallel with TMD stroke — off-the-shelf fluid viscous unit across deck-to-relative motion to add energy dissipation independent of precise tuning
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

concepts.text: Bolted stop angles with elastomeric pads sized beyond 49.4 mm TMD stroke — sacrificial over-travel stops checked for TMD impact load into bracket frame
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

concepts.text: All retrofit hardware confined below soffit line within girder depth — no deck-level change, deck sightline and walkway clearance untouched
concepts.author: Bridge Retrofit Engineer

z2=np.sqrt(3*mu/(8*(1+mu))); k2=w2**2*m; c2=2*z2*np.sqrt(k2*m)
def run(c2v):
    dt=0.002; T=15.0; n=int(T/dt)
    x=np.zeros(n); v=np.zeros(n); y=np.zeros(n); w=np.zeros(n)
    x[0]=0.02; v[0]=0.0; y[0]=0.02; w[0]=0.0
    for i in range(n-1):
        Fk=k1*x[i]+c1*(v[i]); Fk2=k2*(x[i]-y[i])+c2v*((v[i]-w[i]))
        a1=(-k1*x[i]-c1*v[i]-k2*(x[i]-y[i])-c2v*(v[i]-w[i]))/M
        a2=(k2*(x[i]-y[i])+c2v*(v[i]-w[i]))/m
        v[i+1]=v[i]+a1*dt; x[i+1]=x[i]+v[i+1]*dt
        w[i+1]=w[i]+a2*dt; y[i+1]=y[i]+w[i+1]*dt
    return x,y
xb,_=run(0.0)  # placeholder

import math
env0=0.02; envT=abs(x[-1])
zeff=np.log(env0/max(envT,1e-9))/(2*np.pi*f1*15.0)
print(f"k1={k1:.3g} N/m m={m:.0f}kg f2={f2:.3f}Hz z2={z2:.3f} k2={k2:.3g} c2={c2:.3g}")
print(f"bare-ish start 20mm, with-TMD end {abs(x[-1])*1000:.2f}mm zeff~{zeff*100:.1f}%")

evidence.output_full:
Footbridge vertical comfort acceleration limits — from 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri
Setra/HiVoSS vertical serviceability uses acceleration bands around: <0.5 m/s2 maximum comfort, <1.0 m/s2 minimum/mean comfort, >2.5 m/s2 unacceptable. Any footbridge with first vertical mode in the walking step band (~1.5-2.2 Hz) must be checked against these, with dense crowd usually governing.
Evidence: E38 (search: Setra HiVoSS footbridge comfort classes vertical acceleration 0.5 1.0 2.5: WWW.mdpi.com — Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges with Different Shapes of Girders — https://WWW.mdpi.com/2076-3417/10/13/4505)

Pedestrian crowd resonant force model — from 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri
Vertical walking force is modeled as ~700 N body weight with ~280 N (~40%) first harmonic at step resonance. Sparse walkers add linearly, but dense crowd Class III ~0.5 pedestrians/m2 uses imperfect synchronization: equivalent in-phase count Neq ~ 10.8*sqrt(zeta*N) acting together at resonance, producing kN-scale harmonic force and multi-m/s2 bare-deck acceleration when structural damping is ~0.5-1%.
Evidence: E41 (search: Setra footbridge crowd load density synchronized pedestrians equivalent number: mdpi.com — Vibration Serviceability Assessment of a Historic Suspension Footbridge — http://mdpi.com/2075-5309/12/6/732/htm); E42 (search: Setra footbridge crowd load density synchronized pedestrians equivalent number: 1library.net — 4.4.1 Dynamic load cases - Footbridge guide setra — https://1library.net/article/dynamic-load-cases-footbridge-guide-setra.ye693erq); E44 (search: Eurocode pedestrian vertical force harmonic walking frequency: eurocodes.jrc.ec.europa.eu — Microsoft Word - Geradin_JRC_Design of Footbridges_150909.doc — 2021 — https://eurocodes.jrc.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-12/jrc_53442.pdf); E49 (equivalent synchronized pedestrians dense crowd: 5.29); E50 (dense crowd resonant force from equivalent pedestrians: 1.48e+03)

Den Hartog TMD sizing rule for footbridge modes — from 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri
Vertical tuned mass dampers for footbridge first modes typically use mass ratio mu = mTMD/Mmodal ~1-3%. Den Hartog optimum is frequency ratio fTMD/fstruct = 1/(1+mu), i.e. tuned 2-3% below the structure, and TMD damping ratio ~ sqrt(3*mu/(8*(1+mu)^3)) ~0.09-0.10 at mu=0.025. When tuned and damped near optimum, resonant deck acceleration drops by an order of magnitude (>10x) versus the undamped bridge.
Evidence: E12 (search: footbridge tuned mass damper mass ratio tuning Den Hartog: mdpi-res.com — | Article |  | — https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/applsci/applsci-12-06204/article_deploy/applsci-12-06204.pdf); E13 (search: footbridge tuned mass damper mass ratio tuning Den Hartog: backend.orbit.dtu.dk — TMD_nscm19.dvi — https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/files/4682306/TMD_nscm19.pdf); E22 (TMD mass from 2.5 percent ratio: 500); E23 (Den Hartog tuning frequency and damping: (1.85, 0.0933)); E54 (Reaffirm Den Hartog optimum for 500kg TMD on 20t modal mass at 1.9Hz: tmd_mass_kg=500.0 mixed (see keys), tmd_frequency_hz=1.853658536585366 mixed (see keys), tmd_damping_ratio=0.09563650695950075 mixed (see keys), tmd_stiffness_n_m=67824.9078175992 mixed (see keys), tm); E47 (Resonant response with and without TMD to estimate comfort reduction: k1=2.85e+06 c1=1.91e+03 k2=6.76e+04 c2=1.08e+03; a_bare=1.75 a_tmd=0.103 ratio=17; X1=0.7mm X2rel=3.8mm); E51 (dense crowd bare acceleration scaling: 9.26); E52 (dense crowd TMD acceleration scaling: 0.545)

Low-frequency TMD sag versus dynamic stroke regime — from 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri
Modal stiffness scales as k = (2*pi*f)^2*Mmodal, e.g. ~2.85 MN/m for 20 tonne at 1.9 Hz. A low-frequency TMD at ~1.85 Hz is soft, e.g. kTMD = (2*pi*fTMD)^2*mTMD ~68 kN/m for 500 kg, so static sag m*g/kTMD is large ~70 mm. Resonant relative stroke under crowd ~20 mm adds to sag, requiring ~90+ mm working spring compression plus over-travel stops.
Evidence: E11 (modal stiffness from 20 tonne modal mass at 1.9 Hz: 2.85e+06); E24 (TMD stiffness and viscous coefficient: (6.78e+04, 1.09e+03)); E53 (dense crowd stroke scaling: 20.1); E55 (static spring sag under TMD weight: 0.0723); E56 (total spring compression static plus dynamic: 0.0924)

import numpy as np
# Bridge 1.9 Hz, modal mass 20000 kg per E12, k=2.85e6; TMD 800kg f=1.83Hz z=0.12 per E13-E16
f1=1.9; m1=20000.0; k1=2.85e6
m2=800.0; f2=1.83; z2=0.12; k2=1.05e5; c2=2.21e3
w=2*np.pi*f1
# crowd force: Neq~5.92 *280N
F0=5.916*280.0
# bare: zeta 0.5%, retro effective 6.2% per E17
for zeta,label in [(0.005,'bare'),(0.062,'tmd')]:
    c1=2*zeta*np.sqrt(k1*m1)
    # steady-state resonant accel = F0/(2*zeta*m1)
    a=F0/(2*zeta*m1)
    print(label, 'c1=',round(c1,1),' a_ss=',round(a,3),' m/s2 =',round(a/9.81,3),' g')
# time simulation: build-up envelope a(t)=a_ss*(1-exp(-zeta*w*t))
t=np.linspace(0,30,301)
a_bare=F0/(2*0.005*m1)*(1-np.exp(-0.005*w*t))
a_tmd=F0/(2*0.062*m1)*(1-np.exp(-0.062*w*t))
print('t=5s bare',round(float(a_bare[50]),2),'tmd',round(float(a_tmd[50]),2))
print('t=15s bare',round(float(a_bare[150]),2),'tmd',round(float(a_tmd[150]),2))
print('t=30s bare',round(float(a_bare[300]),2),'tmd',round(float(a_tmd[300]),2))
print('comfort: max<0.5 mean 0.5-1.0 min 1.0-2.5 unacceptable>2.5 m/s2')

f2_opt=1.83

F0=1660
# steady state at excitation f1=1.9 Hz with varied f2
w= w1
for err in [-0.05, -0.03, 0.0, 0.03, 0.05]:
    f2=f2_opt*(1+err); k2v=m2*(2*np.pi*f2)**2
    # 2DOF complex
    Z1=k1-m1*w**2+1j*w*0.005*2*m1*w1  # small bare damping approx
    # full matrix solve: [k1+k2-m1w2+icw, -(k2+icw); -(k2+icw), k2-m2w2+icw] [x1;x2]=[F0;0]
    c=c2
    a11=k1+k2v-m1*w**2+1j*w*c
    a12=-(k2v+1j*w*c); a21=a12; a22=k2v-m2*w**2+1j*w*c

    x1=(F0*a22)/det

---
name: tmd-tuning-and-stroke
description: Use when adding a vertical TMD to a low-frequency flexible structure.
source: seeded from knowledge/insights (5 problems) (2026-11-02)
---

## 1. Tune and damp per Den Hartog
1. Select **mass ratio mu=mTMD/Mmodal ~1-3% (example 500 kg on 20 t = 2.5%)** for first vertical mode [run 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri E12,E13,E22].
2. Tune **fTMD/fstruct=1/(1+mu), i.e. 2-3% below structure (example 1.85 Hz for 1.9 Hz)** and damp **zeta~sqrt(3*mu/(8*(1+mu)^3)) ~0.09-0.10 at mu=0.025 (example 0.0933)** [run 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri E12,E13,E23,E54].
3. Verify reduction: near-optimum tuning/damping drops resonant deck acceleration **>10x (example a_bare=1.75 -> a_tmd=0.103 ratio 17; dense 9.26 -> 0.545)** [run 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri E47,E51,E52].

## 2. Size spring for sag plus stroke
4. Compute stiffnesses `k=(2*pi*f)^2*M`: **modal k~2.85 MN/m for 20 t at 1.9 Hz; TMD k~6.78e4 N/m (68 kN/m) with c~1.08-1.09e3 N-s/m for 500 kg at ~1.85 Hz** [run 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri E11,E24,E47].
5. Allow for large static sag plus dynamics: **sag m*g/kTMD ~0.0723 m (72 mm) + resonant relative stroke ~20.1 mm = total ~0.0924 m**, so provide **~90+ mm working compression plus over-travel stops** [run 20261102-121628_vibration-retrofit-for-a-lively-pedestri E55,E53,E56].
